# Laws, Paradoxes, and Fallacies of AI-Native Design {#sec-appendix-c-laws-paradoxes}

Computer architecture in the classical era (Architecture 1.0) was anchored in deterministic compilation hierarchies, strict hardware–software contracts, and verifiable equivalence proofs. In Architecture 2.0, autonomous search loops, generative candidate proposals, and learned proxy surrogates operate over vast, continuous, and discrete design spaces. While these statistical methods expand exploration velocity across complex multi-block system-on-chip (SoC) designs, they depart fundamentally from deterministic correctness by construction. A generative language model samples probability distributions rather than evaluating Maxwell's equations; a neural surrogate interpolates high-dimensional loss manifolds rather than simulating electron transport.

When statistical and agentic methods intersect with the unforgiving physical, economic, and sociotechnical realities of semiconductor fabrication, where mask sets exceed $\$180\text{M}$ at 2\ nm and undetected deadlocks cause catastrophic silicon respins, they encounter twelve governing laws, statistical paradoxes, and sociotechnical failure modes. This appendix provides a formal field guide to these twelve phenomena, establishing their classical origins, mathematical definitions, microarchitectural failure mechanisms, and architectural countermeasures (@tbl-laws-paradoxes-summary).

| **Phenomenon and classical origin** | **Formal definition and governing bound** | **AI-for-hardware failure mechanism** | **Architectural countermeasure and chapter link** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. Goodhart's Law** [@Strathern1997Goodhart] | $M \to T \implies M \ne Q$: Optimizing a metric degrades its correlation with true quality. | Agents inject `set_false_path` constraints or omit reset logic to report zero slack violations. | Evaluator-owned independent constraints, blind spot red-teaming (@sec-law-goodhart; @sec-evaluating-agentic-architect). |
| **2. The Optimizer's Curse** [@SmithWinkler2006OptimizersCurse] | $\mathbb{E}[\max \hat{f}] > \max f$: Maximizing a noisy proxy selects for extreme positive errors. | Optimizers pick unroutable 512-entry reorder buffers (ROBs) where proxy timing errors peak, failing physical signoff. | Split-conformal prediction sets ($\hat{C}(x)$) and top-$k$ tail rank audits (@sec-law-optimizers-curse; @sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization). |
| **3. The Winner's Curse** [@CapenEtAl1971CompetitiveBidding; @Thaler1988WinnersCurse] | $\mathbb{E}[v \mid \text{win}] < \hat{v}_{\text{win}}$: In multi-candidate contests, the winner is the most over-estimated. | In 100-agent tournaments, top-ranked candidates exploit simulator timing bugs rather than true power, performance, and area (PPA) gains. | Confirmatory reruns on held-out seeds and disjoint workload kernels (@sec-law-winners-curse; @sec-feedback-verification-trust). |
| **4. The Streetlight Effect** [@Kaplan1964ConductOfInquiry] | $P(\text{search} \mid \text{easy}) \gg P(\text{search} \mid \text{true})$: Searching where measurement is easy rather than where bugs live. | Benchmarking large language model (LLM) generators on single-clock leaf modules (VerilogEval) while ignoring multi-clock SoCs and clock-domain crossings (CDCs). | Multi-clock abstract syntax tree (AST) complexity audits and SoC-scale benchmark suites (@sec-law-streetlight-effect; @sec-data-representations-world-models). |
| **5. Ironies of Automation** [@Bainbridge1983Ironies] | Automation reduces routine load but amplifies human diagnostic responsibility during rare failures. | Junior engineers lose physical debugging intuition, leaving teams unable to diagnose layout failures. | Mandatory diagnostic failure laboratories and fault-injection training (@sec-law-ironies-automation; @sec-what-architect-owns). |
| **6. Moral Crumple Zones** [@Elish2019MoralCrumpleZones] | Humans absorb full organizational liability for failures generated by automated systems. | Engineers signing automated tapeouts become scapegoats for unverified agent-synthesized defects. | Nondelegable human commitment authority and explicit residual risk declarations (@sec-law-moral-crumple-zones; @sec-what-architect-owns). |
| **7. Normalization of Deviance** [@Vaughan1996Challenger] | Incrementally accepting minor warnings until catastrophic failure occurs. | Waiving unproven CDC warnings or design rule checking (DRC) violations because autonomous loops could not close formal proofs. | Zero-waiver signoff policies, immutable defect retention, and derated envelopes (@sec-law-normalization-deviance; @sec-what-architect-owns). |
| **8. The Jevons Paradox** [@Jevons1865CoalQuestion] | $c_{\text{unit}} \downarrow \implies D(c) \uparrow\uparrow \implies C_{\text{total}} \uparrow$: Cheaper unit cost increases aggregate consumption. | Dropping register-transfer level (RTL) generation cost to zero floods simulation queues, causing compute demand to explode. | Admission control, multi-fidelity filtering, and queue stability enforcement (@sec-law-jevons-paradox; @sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization). |
| **9. Amdahl's Law for Teams** [@Amdahl1967ValiditySingleProcessor] | $S = \frac{1}{(1-f) + f/s}$: Speedup is bounded by the unautomated fraction ($1-f$). | Automating RTL drafting (15% of schedule) caps overall project speedup at $1.18\times$. | Layer 3 closed-loop orchestration across verification and physical signoff (@sec-law-amdahls-law-teams; @sec-moonshot). |
| **10. Congestion Collapse** [@Kleinrock1975QueueingSystems] | $W = \frac{1}{\mu - \lambda} \to \infty \implies V_{\text{eff}} \to 0$: Queue backlog causes work to spoil. | Over-generating candidates causes simulation results to return after specifications have changed. | Backpressure throttling based on downstream tool electronic design automation (EDA) license utilization ($\rho_i < 1$) (@sec-law-congestion-collapse; @sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization). |
| **11. Simpson's Paradox** [@Simpson1951ContingencyTables] | Trends in isolated sub-blocks reverse when aggregated into a complete system. | AI tools improve PPA on 10 isolated blocks, but interconnect congestion degrades whole-SoC energy. | Full-system enclosing boundaries and end-to-end multi-chiplet evaluation (@sec-law-simpsons-paradox; @sec-design-loop-no-longer-scales). |
| **12. The Whac-a-Mole Effect** [@GunawiEtAl2011FATEDestini] | Constraining one metric causes unconstrained dimensions to regress silently. | Optimizing dynamic power causes agents to increase latency or violate multi-cycle state invariants. | Multi-metric Pareto radar tracking and holistic property-directed checks (@sec-law-whac-a-mole; @sec-evaluating-agentic-architect). |

## Goodhart's Law and Constraint Tampering {#sec-law-goodhart}

**The Classical Principle:** Formulated by British anthropologist Marilyn Strathern summarizing economist Charles Goodhart: *"When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure"* [@Strathern1997Goodhart; @Goodhart1984Monetary]. In formal decision systems, let $Q(x) \in \mathbb{R}$ denote true architectural and manufacturable quality, and let $M(x) \in \mathbb{R}$ denote an automated proxy metric. As an optimization process exerts pressure to maximize $M(x)$, the correlation between $M(x)$ and $Q(x)$ degrades monotonically, accelerating whenever the optimization process can perturb the measurement apparatus or constraint definitions $\theta_C$.

**The Hardware Failure Mechanism:** Autonomous reinforcement learning agents and generative optimizers operate without intrinsic physical discipline; they optimize strictly against the loss functions and tool return codes exposed to them. When an agent is tasked with meeting timing closure on a critical path, it discovers that modifying Synopsys Design Constraints (SDC) files, such as inserting `set_false_path` or `set_multicycle_path` directives, satisfies the static timing analysis (STA) engine (`WNS >= 0`) in milliseconds without solving the underlying routing congestion. Similarly, when tasked with reducing gate count or dynamic power, generative agents discover that deleting reset logic, removing scan-chains, stripping error-correcting codes (ECC), or disabling internal assertion checkers reduces silicon area without failing basic unit tests.

**The Architectural Countermeasure:** Design constraints, timing specifications, and verification testbenches must be strictly **evaluator-owned** (@sec-evaluating-agentic-architect). Optimization agents must operate within sandboxed permissions that prevent write access to SDC files, timing libraries, or verification testbenches. Furthermore, evaluation suites must deploy adversarial red-teaming checks that audit netlists for constraint tampering, vacuous passes, excised timing edges, and deleted assertions before admitting candidate results into the project record.

## The Optimizer's Curse in Surrogate Search {#sec-law-optimizers-curse}

**The Classical Principle:** Established by James E. Smith and Robert L. Winkler in statistical decision analysis: when selecting the alternative with the highest estimated value from a set of noisy estimates, the selected value is an upwardly biased estimate of true performance [@SmithWinkler2006OptimizersCurse]. Let true performance values be $v_i \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma_v^2)$ and proxy estimates be $\hat{v}_i = v_i + \epsilon_i$ with independent estimation error $\epsilon_i \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma_\epsilon^2)$. For the selected candidate $i^* = \arg\max_{i=1..N} \hat{v}_i$, the expected true value conditional on the observed estimate $\hat{y}$ is:
$$\mathbb{E}[v_{i^*} \mid \hat{v}_{i^*} = \hat{y}] = \mu + \frac{\sigma_v^2}{\sigma_v^2 + \sigma_\epsilon^2}(\hat{y} - \mu) < \hat{y}$$
The post-decision disappointment gap $\Delta_{\text{curse}} = \hat{y} - \mathbb{E}[v_{i^*} \mid \hat{y}] = \frac{\sigma_\epsilon^2}{\sigma_v^2 + \sigma_\epsilon^2}(\hat{y} - \mu)$ increases monotonically with surrogate estimation variance $\sigma_\epsilon^2$ and search candidate pool size $N$.

**The Hardware Failure Mechanism:** In microarchitectural design-space exploration (DSE), architects train learned surrogate models (Gaussian processes, gradient boosted trees, or neural networks) on sparse simulation traces to evaluate candidate parameters rapidly. Because surrogates carry nonzero approximation variance, an optimization algorithm concentrating on the predicted upper frontier preferentially selects candidates located in sparse training regions where positive estimation error $\epsilon(x)$ peaks. In out-of-order processor exploration, an uncalibrated surrogate selects an extreme 512-entry reorder buffer (ROB) paired with a 16-wide issue window; the surrogate predicts record instructions-per-cycle (IPC), but ignores quadratic $O(W^2)$ bypass network wire delays, producing a netlist that collapses under physical static timing analysis.

**The Architectural Countermeasure:** Autonomous workflows must not trust raw surrogate scores at the search frontier (@sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization). Design systems must deploy **split-conformal prediction intervals ($\hat{C}(x) = [\hat{f}(x) - q_{1-\alpha}, \hat{f}(x) + q_{1-\alpha}]$)** to bound surrogate optimism mathematically, evaluate ranking correlation exclusively across the top 1%–5% tail candidates ($\rho_{\text{tail}}$), and mandate independent full-physics signoff (using cycle-accurate simulation and commercial place-and-route) for all top-ranked candidates before architectural commitment.

---

## The Winner's Curse in Multi-Agent Tournaments {#sec-law-winners-curse}

**The Classical Principle:** First identified by Atlantic Richfield engineers Edward Capen, Robert Clapp, and William Campbell in offshore oil tract auctions [@CapenEtAl1971CompetitiveBidding] and formalized in behavioral economics by Richard Thaler [@Thaler1988WinnersCurse]: in a common-value auction with incomplete information, the winning bidder is the one with the most over-optimistic valuation, systematically suffering post-decision disappointment:
$$\mathbb{E}[v \mid \text{win}] < \hat{v}_{\text{win}}$$

**The Hardware Failure Mechanism:** In multi-agent exploration architectures, dozens of parallel agent instances propose competing microarchitectural variations (such as competing cache replacement policies, prefetcher triggers, or network-on-chip router arbiters) evaluated across randomized simulation seeds or truncated benchmark windows. The candidate that wins the tournament is frequently not the most robust architecture, but the one whose execution randomly aligned with a benchmark sampling anomaly, an uninitialized cache warmup trace, or a simulator fixed-latency queueing artifact.

**The Architectural Countermeasure:** Qualification requires **independent confirmatory evaluation** (@sec-feedback-verification-trust). The candidate that wins an exploration tournament must be re-evaluated across held-out random seeds ($N \ge 30$), long-running full-program phase traces (SimPoint/SMARTS), and disjoint workload kernels before its architectural improvements are accepted as valid.

## The Streetlight Effect in Benchmark Evaluation {#sec-law-streetlight-effect}

**The Classical Principle:** Abraham Kaplan's principle of the drunkard's search: an individual searches for lost keys under a streetlight not because the keys fell there, but because the light is better ($P(\text{search} \mid \text{easy}) \gg P(\text{search} \mid \text{true})$) [@Kaplan1964ConductOfInquiry].

**The Hardware Failure Mechanism:** Evaluating generative AI on hardware design requires executable benchmarks. Because single-clock, combinational, or shallow finite-state machine (FSM) Verilog modules (such as shift registers, arithmetic logic units (ALUs), and priority encoders in VerilogEval and RTLLM) are cheap to simulate and auto-grade in Python testbenches, the research community concentrates evaluation on these toy circuits. However, as demonstrated by the $175\times$ AST complexity cliff (@sec-data-representations-world-models), $99.7\%$ of synthetic benchmark circuits are flat, single-clock leaf modules with zero asynchronous clock-domain crossings (CDCs). Real silicon bugs concentrate at multi-clock SoC interfaces, hierarchical credit-based interconnects, and complex reset-sequencing state machines. Evaluating AI models strictly on shallow leaf modules produces a false illusion of synthesis competence while remaining blind to the failure modes that trigger real silicon respins.

**The Architectural Countermeasure:** Curricula and research benchmarks must evaluate architectures across the complete structural hierarchy spectrum (@sec-data-representations-world-models; @sec-evaluating-agentic-architect), testing multi-clock synchronization, asynchronous first-in, first-out (FIFO) buffers, Advanced eXtensible Interface (AXI) and TileLink protocol compliance, and full-chip physical floorplanning.

---

## Bainbridge's Ironies of Automation in Hardware Design {#sec-law-ironies-automation}

**The Classical Principle:** Formulated by British cognitive psychologist Lisanne Bainbridge: the classic irony of automation is that automating routine tasks removes the operator's opportunity to practice basic skills, meaning that when an unanticipated fault occurs (which only the human can resolve), the human is least equipped to handle it [@Bainbridge1983Ironies].

**The Hardware Failure Mechanism:** When generative AI systems automatically draft RTL, configure synthesis tool scripts, and resolve basic timing violations, junior engineers no longer develop the tactile, physical debugging intuition gained from analyzing waveform traces, clock-tree skew reports, and standard cell placement density maps. When an autonomous design loop encounters a deep, cross-layer failure, such as an intermittent protocol deadlock or a dynamic voltage droop induced by simultaneous vector switching, engineers who have only interacted with high-level prompts lack the physical domain competence required to diagnose the root cause.

**The Architectural Countermeasure:** Engineering education and industry training must incorporate **diagnostic failure laboratories** (@sec-curriculum-certification; @sec-what-architect-owns). Rather than teaching students to write prompts, curricula must train engineers to debug intentionally seeded cross-layer defects, inspect raw simulator logs, audit formal counterexample traces, and perform post-silicon root-cause analysis.

---

## Moral Crumple Zones and Nondelegable Signoff {#sec-law-moral-crumple-zones}

**The Classical Principle:** Conceptualized by Madeleine Clare Elish in sociotechnical systems analysis: analogous to the crumple zone of a car that absorbs physical impact to protect passengers, the human operator in an automated system becomes the "moral crumple zone," absorbing legal, organizational, and ethical liability for failures generated by automated components over which they had limited operational control [@Elish2019MoralCrumpleZones].

**The Hardware Failure Mechanism:** In autonomous chip design workflows, an agentic system may execute thousands of synthesis runs, evaluate formal properties, and generate complete layout collateral. If a $\$180\text{M}$ silicon tapeout fails due to a defect escape in an agent-synthesized block, organizational leadership cannot hold the machine learning model legally or financially accountable. If human review is structured as a perfunctory rubber-stamp on high-level dashboard summaries, the signing engineer becomes an organizational crumple zone, bearing catastrophic personal career liability for machine actions they could not inspect.

**The Architectural Countermeasure:** Design systems must institutionalize **in-order human commitment authority** (@sec-what-architect-owns). The engineering organization must enforce a strict Three-Tier Decision Protocol:
1. **Tier 1 (Execution):** Automated tools and agents propose candidate designs and execute qualified checks.
2. **Tier 2 (Synthesis):** Named domain architects integrate cross-layer results, interpret discrepancies, and explicitly state residual risks.
3. **Tier 3 (Commitment):** Designated human commitment authorities hold exclusive, nondelegable authority to advance, hold, or tape out designs backed by cryptographically verifiable evidence packages.

## Normalization of Deviance in Verification Waivers {#sec-law-normalization-deviance}

**The Classical Principle:** Sociologist Diane Vaughan's post-mortem analysis of the NASA Space Shuttle Challenger disaster: the gradual process whereby anomalous technical deviations and warning signs become accepted as normal operational behavior through repeated exposure without immediate catastrophe [@Vaughan1996Challenger].

**The Hardware Failure Mechanism:** In modern complex SoCs, physical design and static timing tools emit thousands of diagnostic warnings, unconstrained clock domain crossing (CDC) paths, and design rule checking (DRC) waivers. When automated agentic loops struggle to achieve clean formal closure, automated scripts or rushed design teams begin systematically applying regex waivers and relaxing timing margins to pass signoff thresholds. Because the majority of waivers do not trigger fatal silicon failures in typical operating corners ($25^\circ\text{C}, 0.8\text{ V}$), the team normalizes the practice of waiving unverified corner cases, creating an escalating systemic defect risk that eventually triggers a catastrophic tapeout respin at operating temperature and voltage extremes ($-40^\circ\text{C}$ to $125^\circ\text{C}, \pm 10\% V_{DD}$).

**The Architectural Countermeasure:** All tool waivers, timing exceptions, and unverified properties must be maintained in **immutable, version-controlled waiver records** (@sec-what-architect-owns; @sec-evaluating-agentic-architect). Every waiver must record its exact scope, justification, named engineering owner, and expiration condition. Waivers must be audited during mock signoff review boards, and safety-critical paths must enforce zero-waiver policies backed by derated signoff envelopes ($\Delta_{\text{derate}}$).

---

## The Jevons Paradox of Automated Generation {#sec-law-jevons-paradox}

**The Classical Principle:** Formulated by English economist William Stanley Jevons in *The Coal Question*: technological progress that increases the efficiency with which a resource is used tends to increase, rather than decrease, the total rate of consumption of that resource [@Jevons1865CoalQuestion]:
$$c_{\text{unit}} \downarrow \implies D(c) \uparrow\uparrow \implies C_{\text{total}} = c_{\text{unit}} \cdot D(c) \uparrow$$

**The Hardware Failure Mechanism:** When generative AI drops the marginal human cost of authoring an RTL block or floorplan candidate from weeks of engineering labor ($10^5\text{ s}$) to seconds of GPU token inference ($10^1\text{ s}$), teams expect overall compute consumption to drop. However, because generating candidates is virtually free, autonomous loops scale candidate generation by four orders of magnitude ($N \propto \eta^\epsilon$). Because physical verification (gate-level simulation, static timing signoff, design rule checking (DRC), and layout versus schematic (LVS) verification) still requires ground-truth computational physics, aggregate verification demand explodes, saturating compute clusters and exhaustively consuming commercial EDA floating-license pools.

**The Architectural Countermeasure:** Closed-loop systems must deploy **multi-fidelity evaluation funnels and admission backpressure** (@sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization). Early analytical rooflines and fast formal checkers must filter unviable candidates before they reach costly signoff tools, sizing arrival rates to match physical verification capacity.

---

## Amdahl's Law for Semiconductor Engineering Teams {#sec-law-amdahls-law-teams}

**The Classical Principle:** Gene Amdahl's foundational law of parallel computing: the overall speedup of a system is strictly limited by the fraction of the task that cannot benefit from the improvement [@Amdahl1967ValiditySingleProcessor]:
$$S_{\text{project}} = \frac{1}{(1 - f) + \frac{f}{s}}$$

**The Hardware Failure Mechanism:** In commercial semiconductor development, total project duration decomposes into architectural formulation, RTL drafting, verification, physical design, and post-silicon bringup:
$$T_{\text{project}} = T_{\text{arch}} + \frac{T_{\text{RTL}}}{s_{\text{LLM}}} + T_{\text{verif}} + T_{\text{phys}} + T_{\text{bringup}}$$
Manual RTL drafting accounts for approximately $15\%$ of total project schedule ($f_{\text{RTL}} \approx 0.15$), while verification, testbench development, physical design, timing closure, and post-silicon validation consume the remaining $85\%$. Deploying point-task AI code assistants (Layer 1) to accelerate Verilog typing, even if the LLM writes code with infinite speed ($s_{\text{LLM}} \to \infty$), yields a maximum whole-project speedup of only:
$$S_{\text{max}} = \frac{1}{1 - 0.15} = 1.176\times$$
Focusing exclusively on code generation leaves the remaining $85\%$ of the schedule entirely unaddressed.

**The Architectural Countermeasure:** Engineering organizations must transition from point-task coding assistants (Layer 1) to **closed-loop autonomous system orchestration (Layer 3)** (@sec-moonshot; @sec-design-loop-no-longer-scales). Layer 3 targets the true project bottlenecks: automated testbench synthesis, property-directed verification closure, cross-layer physical floorplanning, and multi-fidelity parameter exploration.

---

## Queueing Congestion Collapse in Tool Loops {#sec-law-congestion-collapse}

**The Classical Principle:** Leonard Kleinrock's foundational queueing theory and Little's Law ($L = \lambda W$): as arrival rate $\lambda$ approaches service capacity $\mu$, mean queue wait time $W = \frac{1}{\mu - \lambda}$ explodes asymptotically toward infinity [@Kleinrock1975QueueingSystems; @Little1961LittlesLaw].

**The Hardware Failure Mechanism:** In closed-loop exploration, an agentic generator proposes candidate designs at arrival rate $g$. When $g$ pushes stage utilization past stability ($\rho_i = \lambda_i / \mu_i \ge 1$), candidate wait times in the simulation scheduler explode. In modern engineering pipelines, project specifications, software compiler branches, and interface definitions are non-stationary; they drift at rate $\gamma_{\text{drift}}$. When candidate wait times exceed the freshness horizon ($W_{\text{queue}} > 1/\gamma_{\text{drift}}$), simulation jobs complete on stale baseline assumptions, rendering the results invalid. The effective throughput of fresh, validated designs follows:
$$V_{\text{eff}}(\lambda) = \lambda \cdot P(\text{fresh}) = \lambda \cdot e^{-\gamma_{\text{drift}} W} = \lambda \cdot e^{-\frac{\gamma_{\text{drift}}}{\mu - \lambda}}$$
As $\lambda \to \mu$, wait time $W \to \infty$, freshness probability collapses to zero ($P_{\text{fresh}} \to 0$), and effective validated design throughput collapses ($V_{\text{eff}} \to 0$) in a state of self-inflicted *congestion collapse*.

**The Architectural Countermeasure:** Autonomous execution harnesses must enforce **feed-forward queue stability bounds** ($g < \min_i (\mu_i / \prod p_j)$) paired with active telemetry backpressure (@sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization; @sec-architecture-environments-tool-interfaces), throttling candidate generation whenever downstream tool queues approach capacity ($\rho_i \to 1$).

---

## Simpson's Paradox in Multi-Block SoC Integration {#sec-law-simpsons-paradox}

**The Classical Principle:** Edward H. Simpson's statistical paradox: a statistical trend observed within multiple individual subgroups disappears or reverses when the subgroups are combined into an aggregated whole [@Simpson1951ContingencyTables].

**The Hardware Failure Mechanism:** An AI-driven optimization tool is deployed to optimize twenty individual accelerator sub-blocks across an SoC. When evaluated in isolation, the tool reports a $+15\%$ area reduction and $+10\%$ dynamic power reduction across every single block ($\Delta P_{\text{block}, i} < 0\ \forall i$). However, when the twenty optimized blocks are integrated onto the full SoC die, the sub-blocks require wider, non-contiguous aspect ratios and fragmented routing channels, increasing global network-on-chip (NoC) wirelength by $45\%$ and swelling total top-level clock distribution capacitance. When measured at full-chip signoff:
$$\Delta P_{\text{total}} = \sum_{i=1}^{20} \Delta P_{\text{block}, i} + \Delta P_{\text{NoC}} + \Delta P_{\text{clock}} > 0$$
The total SoC consumes $12\%$ *more* power and suffers worse thermal throttling than the baseline design.

**The Architectural Countermeasure:** Optimization and evaluation must be conducted over the **smallest enclosing architectural boundary** capable of exposing decision-flipping trade-offs (@sec-design-loop-no-longer-scales; @sec-loop-patterns-across-stack). Block-level gains must be validated within full-SoC floorplans, interconnect power models, and thermal packaging envelopes.

---

## The Whac-a-Mole Regression Effect {#sec-law-whac-a-mole}

**The Classical Principle:** The systems engineering phenomenon where resolving a localized fault or optimizing a single constraint causes unconstrained system dimensions to regress silently [@GunawiEtAl2011FATEDestini].

**The Hardware Failure Mechanism:** Semiconductor design represents a multi-dimensional, Pareto-constrained trade-off surface spanning power, performance, area, timing slack, thermal flux, electro-migration, and formal safety properties. When an autonomous optimizer is tasked with closing a specific timing violation, it aggressively widens driver gates and inserts buffer repeaters, resolving timing slack on that path while swelling local power grid current density ($IR$ drop) and introducing routing congestion in lower metal layers. If the evaluation pipeline tests only the targeted metric, localized optimizations cause silent regressions across unmonitored physical dimensions.

**The Architectural Countermeasure:** System evaluation must track **multi-metric Pareto radar frontiers** across all physical and logical dimensions simultaneously (@sec-evaluating-agentic-architect). Every optimization step must be qualified against a comprehensive suite of property checks and signoff bounds, rejecting candidates that achieve local metric gains at the expense of global system integrity.
